stem: A patient undergoes maxillofacial surgery, during which the surgeon accidentally injures the facial nerve. Which of the following muscles is affected:
fact: The buccinator is innervated by the facial nerve; the other listed muscles are supplied by V3 or IX.
mnemonic: VII moves the cheek; V3 moves the jaw.
finding: Source answer page displays buccinator as correct.

stem: The oculomotor nerve supplies all of the following muscles EXCEPT for the:
fact: CN III supplies the listed muscles except lateral rectus, which is supplied by CN VI.
mnemonic: LR6: lateral rectus is CN VI; most other eye muscles are III.
finding: Source page displays lateral rectus as the exception.

stem: The vagus nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: The vagus nerve exits the skull through the jugular foramen.
mnemonic: IX, X, XI travel through the jugular foramen.
finding: Source page displays jugular foramen as correct.

stem: Regarding the olfactory nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The olfactory bulb lies in the posterior cranial fossa.
The olfactory nerve is the longest cranial nerve.
The olfactory nerve originates from the medulla oblongata.
The olfactory nerve carries crude touch sensation from the nasal cavity.
The olfactory tract runs inferiorly to the frontal lobe.
fact: The olfactory tract lies inferior to the frontal lobe; CN I enters through the cribriform plate and the bulb lies in the anterior cranial fossa.
mnemonic: I smells under the frontal lobe.
finding: Source page displays the inferior olfactory-tract course as correct.

stem: Regarding the vagus nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The vagus nerve is a motor and sensory nerve.
The vagus nerve originates in the medulla.
The vagus nerve exits the skull via the jugular foramen.
It is the afferent nerve of the gag reflex.
It innervates the palatoglossal muscle of the tongue.
fact: CN IX is the afferent limb and CN X is the efferent limb of the gag reflex; the other statements are compatible with the vagus nerve.
finding: Source page displays the afferent-gag statement as incorrect.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the corneal blink reflex:
fact: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve is the afferent limb of the corneal blink reflex; CN VII is efferent.
mnemonic: V1 feels the cornea; VII closes the lids.
finding: Source page displays ophthalmic nerve as correct.

stem: Which of the following features is NOT typical of oculomotor (CN III) palsy:
fact: CN III palsy causes ptosis, pupil dilation, accommodation impairment, and a down-and-out eye; inability to abduct is due to CN VI palsy.
mnemonic: III palsy is down and out; VI palsy cannot look out.
finding: Source page displays inability to abduct as not typical.

stem: A 64 year old man presents to ED with progressive hearing loss in his left ear, together with drooping of his left lip and complaints of food collecting in his left oral vestibule. Imaging shows a tumour compressing which of the following structures:
fact: The facial and vestibulocochlear nerves pass through the internal acoustic meatus, explaining facial weakness with hearing loss.
mnemonic: Internal acoustic meatus carries VII and VIII.
finding: Source page displays internal acoustic meatus as correct.
